name: Aardwolf Core
author: Solao
description: GMCP negotiation and session bootstrap. Required by the other Aardwolf panels.
script:
--[[ aw-core.lua Sean Stoves (Solao) — 2026-08-03 Session bootstrap for the Aardwolf UI. Negotiates the GMCP options the panels depend on and primes the server into resending current state. Two things make this necessary: - Aardwolf's group monitor is OFF by default. Nothing gets a group packet until either "Group 1" is in Core.Supports.Set or a literal 'group on' is sent. Other plugins declare what they need and Core sends the union: broadcastPlugin("aw-gmcp", "Char,Room") See docs/CORE.md for the contract, and docs/MUDFORGE-NOTES.md for the runtime and sanitiser behaviour every plugin here has had to work around. ]] plugin = { id = "aw-core", name = "Aardwolf Core", version = "1.16.0", author = "Solao", description = "GMCP negotiation and session bootstrap. Required by the other Aardwolf panels.", settings = { saveState = true }, } -- @category utilities --[[ Every diagnostic line carries the running version. Chasing a bug that was already fixed on disk cost several rounds — the output has to say which build is actually answering. ]] local TAG = "$Y[Core v" .. plugin.version .. "]$w " local TAGR = "$R[Core v" .. plugin.version .. "]$w " --[[ The supports list is built from what the loaded plugins actually ask for, not hardcoded at its maximum. Core.Supports.Set REPLACES the server's record rather than merging into it, so exactly one plugin may ever send it — this one. Everything else declares what it needs and Core sends the union: broadcastPlugin("aw-gmcp", "Char,Room") A comma-separated string, deliberately, not a table: arrays crossing the plugin boundary have arrived 0-indexed, undefined, or as JSON objects with numeric keys more than once in this codebase. A string can't. The union is persisted, because Core may well load before the plugins that need things — on the next login it already knows the full set rather than starting narrow and widening after everything else has registered. Aardwolf rejects anything outside this set with "unsupported keyword". ]] local VALID = { core = "Core", char = "Char", comm = "Comm", room = "Room", group = "Group" } --[[ A usable string, or nil. JS undefined reaching a string field arrives as the literal text "undefined" and is truthy besides, so `x or default` never fires on it. ]] local function str(v) if type(v) ~= "string" then return nil end if v == "" or v == "undefined" or v == "null" then return nil end return v end --[[ The id of the room we're standing in. getCurrentRoom() returns the room RECORD — a 14-field table — while getPlayerRoom() returns the number. Passing the table to gotoRoom and getRoomArea is why every attempt to nudge the map view did nothing, and why the diagnostic printed "for room [object Object]" with every reader nil. ]] local function here_id() local ok, v = pcall(function() return getPlayerRoom() end) if ok and tonumber(v) then return tonumber(v) end ok, v = pcall(function() return getCurrentRoom() end) if ok then if tonumber(v) then return tonumber(v) end if type(v) == "table" and tonumber(v.num) then return tonumber(v.num) end end return nil end --[[ A real number, or nil. type(x) == "number" isn't enough on its own: NaN is a number and prints as "NaN", which is exactly what a missing field did to the import panel's counters. ]] local function num(v) local n = tonumber(v) if type(n) ~= "number" then return nil end if n ~= n then return nil end return n end --[[ Baseline. Core is never optional, and neither is Room: MudForge's own mapper reads room.info and is not a plugin, so it can't declare a need. Leaving Room to whichever plugin happens to want it means disabling that plugin silently kills the map — the exact failure this whole one-owner arrangement exists to prevent. ]] local BASELINE = { Core = true, Room = true } --[[ Declarations kept per plugin, not merged straight into a set. A merged set can only grow: disable a plugin and its packages stay subscribed forever, which defeats asking for only what's needed. Keyed by the plugin that asked, the union can be rebuilt from whoever is actually loaded — so removing a plugin narrows the list on the next rebuild. ]] local declared = {} -- [pluginId] = "Char,Room" local needs = { Core = true, Room = true } --[[ Aardwolf's own commands are not JSON — they go over as bare strings. sendGMCP(package) with no data argument passes the string through untouched, the equivalent of MUSHclient's 'sendgmcp group on'. ]] local OPTIONS = { "group on", -- group monitor, needed by the group panel } --[[ 'gmcpchannels on' is NOT sent by default, and this is the important bit: Aardwolf's own doc says it makes channels go over GMCP *only*, which is a server-side gag on every channel at once. Channel text simply stops arriving in the main window, no matter what the Comms panel is set to — which is exactly the "gagging when unchecked" behaviour it caused. comm.channel does NOT depend on it. GMCP channel messages come from "Comm 1" in the supports list, which is always sent; this option only adds the suppression on top. Left off so channels appear in both places, which is the sane default. Anyone who wants the terminal quiet can turn it on here rather than gagging channel by channel. ]] local gmcpOnly = false --[[ Asked for after the options land, so the panels get a full state dump instead of waiting for the next natural change. 'request char' is deliberately NOT here. It makes Aardwolf resend char.*, including char.base — which is the very packet this plugin bootstraps on. That closes a loop: request char -> char.base -> bootstrap -> request char, forever, at whatever rate the server answers. It ran away exactly like that on a live session. Room and quest don't feed back, so they're safe. The manual /awcore path still asks for char, because by then the latch is already set and the reply can't re-trigger anything. ]] local REQUESTS = { "request room", "request quest", } local debugOn = false local quiet = false --[[ MudForge refuses to create a timer while the session is disconnected — "Cannot add timer - not connected to server". The importer is driven entirely by setTimeout, so starting one at the login prompt produced a run that reported itself as running and never advanced a single row. ]] local connected = false --[[ Core has no panel of its own — it's protocol plumbing. Rather than park a permanent widget on screen for a handful of toggles, the settings window is created hidden and summoned with /awcore. ]] local panel = nil local shown = false --[[ Hand-rolled JSON array, deliberately. Passing a Lua table to sendGMCP sends {"1":"Core 1","2":"Char 1",...} — a JSON *object* with numeric keys. Lua arrays are 1-indexed, and MudForge transpiles to JavaScript rather than running a VM, so the table comes out the other side as an object, not an array. Aardwolf rejects that outright ("expected element to be string"), which means the whole subscription silently never takes. sendGMCP passes a string argument through untouched, so build the array text ourselves and let it go as-is. ]] -- stable order, so an unchanged set produces an identical string and the -- change check below doesn't fire on table iteration order alone local function supports_list() local out = {} for _, name in ipairs({ "Core", "Char", "Comm", "Room", "Group" }) do if needs[name] then table.insert(out, name .. " 1") end end return out end local function supports_json() local parts = {} for _, pkg in ipairs(supports_list()) do table.insert(parts, '"' .. pkg .. '"') end -- Makes Aardwolf echo its own GMCP parse errors back to us. Worth having -- while wiring up a new panel, noisy the rest of the time. if debugOn then table.insert(parts, '"debug 1"') end return "[" .. table.concat(parts, ",") .. "]" end --[[ char.base fires more than once per login, and we subscribe under both casings, so an unguarded handler re-sends the whole sequence several times per connect — four Core.Supports.Set in a row on the last run. Latch it, and only re-arm on disconnect or an explicit /awcore. ]] local booted = false local lastRun = 0 -- Hard floor between negotiations, latch or no latch. If anything ever -- re-opens a feedback loop, this caps it at one round per interval instead -- of letting it run at whatever rate the server answers. local MIN_GAP_MS = 5000 local function bootstrap(why, force) if booted and not force then return end local now = getCurrentTime() if lastRun > 0 and (now - lastRun) < MIN_GAP_MS then return end booted = true lastRun = now sendGMCP("Core.Supports.Set", supports_json()) for _, opt in ipairs(OPTIONS) do sendGMCP(opt) end -- explicitly off unless asked for, so a stale server-side setting from an -- earlier session gets cleared rather than lingering sendGMCP(gmcpOnly and "gmcpchannels on" or "gmcpchannels off") for _, req in ipairs(REQUESTS) do sendGMCP(req) end -- safe here only because the latch is already set, so the char.* reply -- can't come back around and re-trigger us if force then sendGMCP("request char") end --[[ One line, and silenceable. Note this is only ours — the "GMCP Sent:" echo above it is MudForge's own protocol debug, turned off under Settings -> Debug, not from here. ]] if not quiet then utilprint(TAG .. "GMCP ready (" .. why .. ")") end end --[[ Tag-based output (statmon and friends) goes here once the panels that need it exist. Deliberately not stubbed with guessed commands. ]] --[[ Command args arrive from JavaScript, where arrays start at 0 while Lua expects 1 — so args[1] is the SECOND word. Normalise before reading. ]] local function argv(args) local out = {} --[[ The runtime may hand over the raw argument string instead of a table. Indexing that yields characters, not words — args[1] off "sex male" is "e", which is how '/avatar sex male' ended up validating "e" as a URL and '/awgroup autohide' fell through to the debug dump. Split by hand: the string library runs on JS regex, so Lua character classes can't be trusted here. ]] if type(args) == "string" then local out, cur = {}, "" for i = 1, string.len(args) do local c = string.sub(args, i, i) if c == " " or c == "\t" then if cur ~= "" then table.insert(out, cur); cur = "" end else cur = cur .. c end end if cur ~= "" then table.insert(out, cur) end return out end if type(args) ~= "table" then return out end local i = 0 while args[i] ~= nil do table.insert(out, tostring(args[i])) i = i + 1 end if #out == 0 then for _, v in ipairs(args) do table.insert(out, tostring(v)) end end return out end local CSS = [[ ]] local function chip(action, label, on) return '
' .. label .. '
' end ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ -- MUSHclient map importer -- -- Brings a MUSHclient Aardwolf mapper database into MudForge's mapper. -- -- The SQLite half happens outside the client — tools/import-mushmap.py turns -- Aardwolf.db into numbered Lua chunks under libs/, because a plugin can't -- open a database file and there is no JSON parser in the sandbox either. -- All that crosses over is Lua source, which require() already handles. -- -- 23k rooms and 76k exits is far too much for one pass. Doing it in a loop -- would wedge the client for however long it took, so the work runs on a -- TIME budget rather than a row count: each tick applies rows until it has -- spent IMP_BUDGET milliseconds, then hands the UI back for IMP_GAP. A slow -- machine does fewer rows per tick and takes longer; it never stops -- responding. That's the whole reason there's no batch-size setting. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ local IMP_BUDGET = 20 -- ms of work per tick local IMP_GAP = 15 -- ms handed back to the client between ticks --[[ The same pause, expressed for addTimer, whose units are undocumented. An integer, and specifically 1. 0.05 was tried on the theory that it reads sanely as either seconds or milliseconds; it produced no second tick at all, which is what a fractional interval floored to zero and rejected looks like. 1 is valid under either reading — one millisecond or one second — and the per-tick budget below adapts to whichever it turns out to be. ]] local IMP_GAP_T = 1 local imp = { running = false, phase = 1, chunk = 1, row = 1, rows = nil, -- chunk currently being applied done = 0, total = 0, errs = 0, started = 0, phases = nil, area = {}, -- Aardwolf area key -> MudForge area id title = {}, -- Aardwolf area key -> the area's readable name env = {}, -- terrain name -> environment id note = "", mode = "import", -- "import" | "wipe" armed = false, -- the wipe asks twice; it can't be undone } -- MUSHclient stores environment colour as an ANSI index, so it needs a palette -- to become the RGB that setCustomEnvColor wants local ANSI_RGB = { [0] = {0,0,0}, [1] = {170,0,0}, [2] = {0,170,0}, [3] = {170,85,0}, [4] = {0,0,170}, [5] = {170,0,170}, [6] = {0,170,170}, [7] = {170,170,170}, [8] = {85,85,85}, [9] = {255,85,85}, [10] = {85,255,85}, [11] = {255,255,85}, [12] = {85,85,255}, [13] = {255,85,255},[14] = {85,255,255},[15] = {255,255,255}, } --[[ Everything that writes to the map goes through these four. Kept together on purpose: the API is undocumented and these signatures are read off the Mudlet compatibility layer, so if one of them is wrong this is the only place to correct. '/awcore import probe' exercises each on a scratch room and reports, which is worth doing before a 23k-room run. ]] local function map_room(r) local id = tonumber(r.uid) if not id then return end if not roomExists(id) then addRoom(id) end if type(r.name) == "string" and r.name ~= "" then setRoomName(id, r.name) end local aid = imp.area[r.area or ""] if aid == nil then aid = str(r.area) end if aid ~= nil then setRoomArea(id, aid) end local env = imp.env[string.lower(r.terrain or "")] if env then setRoomEnv(id, env) end --[[ Always positioned now, and negatives are fine. MUSHclient only stored coordinates for 8,806 of 22,951 rooms — its mapper works the layout out from the exits every time it draws and never writes most of it down. Aylor had 285 rooms and one coordinate pair between them, so the imported map had nothing to place and drew the five rooms it had walked itself. tools/import-mushmap.py now walks each area and assigns a grid position per exit, so every room arrives with one. ]] if type(r.x) == "number" then setRoomCoordinates(id, r.x, r.y or 0, r.z or 0) end local title = imp.title[r.area or ""] if type(title) == "string" and title ~= "" then setRoomUserData(id, "aard.area", title) end --[[ Mark it seen. The map's room records carry lastVisited and timesVisited, and imported rooms had neither — every sampled record showed NaN in that position. The renderer draws the room you're in and the ones you've actually walked, and puts exit STUBS where a neighbour exists but isn't drawn, which is exactly the picture: two rooms and four orange arrows in an area holding two hundred. Guarded because updateMapRoom's shape is a guess; if it doesn't take, the import is no worse off than it already was. ]] if type(updateMapRoom) == "function" and type(getMapRoom) == "function" then pcall(function() --[[ REPLACES, doesn't merge. Handing it just the two fields returned true and left the room with area=NaN, zone=NaN and terrain=17 — every other field gone. So read the record, add to it, and write the whole thing back. It costs a read per room. That's the price of an API that answers "true" to a call that destroyed the row. ]] local rec = getMapRoom(id) if type(rec) ~= "table" then return end local merged = {} for k, v in pairs(rec) do merged[k] = v end merged.timesVisited = 1 merged.lastVisited = getCurrentTime() updateMapRoom(id, merged) end) end if type(r.info) == "string" and r.info ~= "" then setRoomUserData(id, "aard.flags", r.info) end if type(r.notes) == "string" and r.notes ~= "" then setRoomUserData(id, "aard.notes", r.notes) end end local function map_exit(e) return setExit(e.f, e.t, e.d) end --[[ A door is a normal exit you have to open first. Both halves are kept: the exit so pathfinding can route through it, and the command so a walker can send 'open east' before moving. MUSHclient stored the whole sequence because it splits on ';' when sending; MudForge may not, so the raw string is parked in room user data rather than fired blind. ]] local function map_door(e) local ok = setExit(e.f, e.t, e.d) setRoomUserData(e.f, "aard.door." .. tostring(e.d), e.c) if type(setDoor) == "function" then pcall(function() setDoor(e.f, e.d, 1) end) end return ok end --[[ addSpecialExit(from, COMMAND, to). Measured, not guessed. The Mudlet-sounding (from, to, command) returns false and leaves getSpecialExits empty; with the command in the middle it returns true and the exit is there. Every import before this silently skipped all 192 portals, reporting no errors, because a false return isn't a thrown error and nothing was checking it. ]] local function map_special(e) return addSpecialExit(e.f, e.c, e.t) end ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ local function imp_index() local ok, ix = pcall(require, "awmap-index") if not ok or type(ix) ~= "table" then return nil end return ix end --[[ Chunks are re-copied through ipairs rather than indexed where they land. A table that came back from require() has crossed the Lua-to-JavaScript boundary and indexing it directly is exactly the 0-vs-1 trap that has bitten every other array in this codebase. ipairs is proven, and rebuilding through table.insert gives something our own numeric indexing can be trusted on. ]] local function imp_load(file) local ok, mod = pcall(require, file) if not ok or type(mod) ~= "table" then return nil end local rows = {} for _, v in ipairs(mod) do table.insert(rows, v) end return rows end --[[ The next row to apply, advancing chunk and phase as needed. nil means the whole job is finished. ]] local function imp_next() while true do local ph = imp.phases and imp.phases[imp.phase] if type(ph) ~= "table" then return nil, nil end if type(imp.rows) == "table" then local row = imp.rows[imp.row] if type(row) == "table" then imp.row = imp.row + 1 return row, ph end imp.rows = nil imp.chunk = imp.chunk + 1 imp.row = 1 elseif type(ph.inline) == "table" then -- rows handed over directly (the wipe builds its list at runtime -- rather than reading it off disk). One pass, then next phase. if imp.chunk == 1 then imp.rows = ph.inline else imp.phase = imp.phase + 1 imp.chunk = 1 imp.row = 1 end else local file = ph.files and ph.files[imp.chunk] if type(file) ~= "string" then imp.phase = imp.phase + 1 imp.chunk = 1 imp.row = 1 else imp.rows = imp_load(file) if imp.rows == nil then imp.errs = imp.errs + 1 imp.chunk = imp.chunk + 1 end end end end end local function imp_save() saveTable("aw_import", { phase = imp.phase, chunk = imp.chunk, row = imp.row, done = imp.done, errs = imp.errs, total = imp.total, }) end local imp_render = nil -- defined below; the tick needs it --[[ Get the map view to notice what we just wrote. The rows land in storage — 214 rooms became 22,974 — but the widget draws from whatever it loaded at startup, so a finished import leaves an empty map on screen looking exactly like a failed one. Which of these actually reloads it isn't documented, so all of them get a turn: redraw, then re-point at the room the player is standing in, which is what forces the surrounding area to be fetched. ]] local function imp_repaint() for _, fn in ipairs({ "refreshMap", "updateMap" }) do if type(_G[fn]) == "function" then pcall(_G[fn]) end end local here = here_id() if not here then return end if type(setAreaView) == "function" and type(getRoomArea) == "function" then pcall(function() setAreaView(getRoomArea(here)) end) end if type(gotoRoom) == "function" then pcall(function() gotoRoom(here) end) end end local function imp_finish(why) imp.running = false imp.note = why or "done" local secs = math.floor((getCurrentTime() - imp.started) / 1000) utilprint(TAG .. "import " .. imp.note .. ": " .. imp.done .. " row(s) in " .. secs .. "s" .. (imp.errs > 0 and (", " .. imp.errs .. " error(s)") or "") .. ".") imp_repaint() --[[ Say the quiet part. The rows are in storage the moment they're written, but the map widget builds its model when the client starts and none of refreshMap, updateMap, setAreaView or gotoRoom has been enough to make it re-read. Until that's understood, a restart is the reliable step — and not saying so leaves a finished import looking like a failed one. ]] if imp.mode ~= "wipe" then utilprint(TAG .. "restart MudForge to see it. The map view is built at " .. "startup and doesn't re-read what an import just wrote.") end --[[ A row that didn't throw isn't proof it landed — a writer could no-op just as quietly. Ask the mapper what it holds now and print that. ]] if type(getMapStats) == "function" then local sok, st = pcall(getMapStats) if sok and type(st) == "table" then local bits = {} for k, v in pairs(st) do table.insert(bits, tostring(k) .. "=" .. tostring(v)) end if #bits > 0 then utilprint(TAG .. "map now holds: " .. table.concat(bits, ", ")) end end end imp_save() if imp_render then imp_render() end end --[[ Forward declaration, and it is load-bearing. imp_schedule() calls imp_tick, which is defined below it. Without this the name resolves to a GLOBAL imp_tick — nil — and setTimeout(nil, 15) schedules nothing at all: the run reports itself as started and never advances a row, with no error anywhere. ]] local imp_tick = nil --[[ Queue the next tick, or stand down until there's a connection to hang a timer off. Resuming is automatic: onConnect picks it back up, so walking away at the password prompt costs nothing. ]] --[[ The client's own timer, and nothing else. An earlier version also drove ticks off onLine, after setTimeout refused with "Cannot add timer - not connected to server" during a session MudForge had wrongly flagged as disconnected. That was a workaround for a client bug dressed up as a feature: it made progress depend on the game saying something, so an idle prompt looked identical to a broken import. Timers work when the session is genuinely connected. If they ever stop, the watchdog below says so rather than quietly limping along on output. ]] --[[ The client's timers — but not just the one. setTimeout has gone completely dead in a live session more than once: "Cannot add timer - not connected to server" while the game is plainly answering, and the watchdog never fires either, because it is itself a setTimeout. addTimer is a separate call and may or may not share the fate. So the first tick arms BOTH, and whichever fires first claims the job; every tick after that uses only the winner. Arming both forever would double the tick rate each round, which is why this locks in. ]] local function imp_schedule() local d = imp.driver if d == "setTimeout" then pcall(function() setTimeout(imp_tick, IMP_GAP) end) return end if d == "addTimer" then pcall(function() addTimer(IMP_GAP_T, imp_tick, false) end) return end if type(setTimeout) == "function" then pcall(function() setTimeout(function() if imp.driver == nil then imp.driver = "setTimeout" end imp_tick() end, IMP_GAP) end) end if type(addTimer) == "function" then pcall(function() addTimer(IMP_GAP_T, function() if imp.driver == nil then imp.driver = "addTimer" end imp_tick() end, false) end) end end imp_tick = function() if not imp.running then return end if imp.inTick == true then return end imp.inTick = true imp.ticks = (num(imp.ticks) or 0) + 1 local start = getCurrentTime() local since = 0 local step = num(imp.step) or 1 --[[ Work scales to the gap the timer actually gives us. 20ms of work every 35ms is right for a millisecond timer. If addTimer turns out to mean seconds, that same 20ms every second is 99,262 rows at 289 a tick — nearly six minutes of watching a bar crawl. Hold the work to a fifth of the observed gap instead: the client stays as responsive either way, and a coarse timer simply does more per visit. ]] local budget = IMP_BUDGET local gap = num(imp.gapMs) if gap and gap > 100 then budget = math.floor(gap / 5) if budget > 250 then budget = 250 end end while true do local row, ph = imp_next() if row == nil then imp.inTick = false imp_finish("complete") return end -- one bad row must not take the run down with it; 76k rows means -- something in there will be malformed --[[ false counts as failure, not just a thrown error. addSpecialExit returned false for every portal across several full imports and each one was recorded as a success, because pcall only catches throws. A writer that answers "no" is a writer that failed. ]] local ok, res = pcall(function() return ph.apply(row) end) if not ok or res == false then imp.errs = imp.errs + 1 end imp.done = imp.done + 1 since = since + 1 if since >= step then local spent = getCurrentTime() - start since = 0 --[[ The stride between clock reads has to be earned, not assumed. It was a flat 25, on the reasoning that reading the clock every row would itself cost real time. True for the import, where a row is a handful of property writes — and badly wrong for the wipe, where deleteRoom has to unpick the room's connections out of 73,000 of them. Twenty-five of those before the first look at the clock is seconds of frozen client per tick, which is exactly what a 20ms budget was supposed to prevent. So it starts at one and grows only while the rows keep proving they're cheap, and backs off when they stop being. ]] if spent >= budget then if spent > (budget * 2) and step > 1 then step = math.floor(step / 2) end imp.step = step break end if step < 256 and spent < (budget / 4) then step = step * 2 end imp.step = step end end --[[ Clear the re-entrancy guard. Losing this line is why every run managed exactly one tick and stopped: the flag is set on entry, the guard at the top returns early while it's set, so tick two and everything after it returned instantly. It looked like a dead timer for three rounds. ]] imp.inTick = false if imp.ticks == 1 then utilprint(TAG .. "running on " .. tostring(imp.driver or "?") .. ".") end if num(imp.lastTickAt) then imp.gapMs = getCurrentTime() - imp.lastTickAt if imp.ticks == 2 then utilprint(TAG .. math.floor(imp.gapMs) .. "ms between ticks.") end end imp.lastTickAt = getCurrentTime() if imp_render then imp_render() end imp_save() imp_schedule() end --[[ Build the phase list from the index. Order matters: areas and environments first because rooms reference them, rooms before exits because an exit to a room that doesn't exist yet is dropped, and special exits last. ]] local function imp_plan() local ix = imp_index() if not ix then return nil end local phases = {} --[[ Areas are registered under the Aardwolf area KEY, not its title. MudForge stores a room's area as the zone string, and the zone it gets from room.info is the key — 'aylor', not 'The Grand City of Aylor'. Registering the title created a parallel set of areas the live mapper never looks at: 22,974 rooms in storage and the map still drawing the five it had walked, because the room you were standing in was in 'aylor' and every imported neighbour was in 'The Grand City of Aylor'. The title is kept on each room as user data, so nothing is lost. ]] table.insert(phases, { name = "areas", files = { "awmap-areas" }, n = ix.areas or 0, apply = function(a) local key = a.uid if type(key) ~= "string" or key == "" then return end --[[ Whatever addAreaName returns is what setRoomArea wants back. It is NOT a numeric id — the probe has it returning the area NAME — and running it through tonumber() gave nil, so imp.area stayed empty and setRoomArea was never called for a single one of the 22,946 rooms. Take it verbatim. ]] local ok, ref = pcall(function() return addAreaName(key) end) if ok and ref ~= nil then imp.area[key] = ref else imp.area[key] = key end imp.title[key] = a.name end }) table.insert(phases, { name = "terrain", files = { "awmap-envs" }, n = ix.envs or 0, apply = function(v) local id = tonumber(v.uid) if not id then return end imp.env[string.lower(v.name or "")] = id local rgb = ANSI_RGB[tonumber(v.color) or 7] if rgb and type(setCustomEnvColor) == "function" then setCustomEnvColor(id, rgb[1], rgb[2], rgb[3], 255) end end }) table.insert(phases, { name = "rooms", files = ix.roomFiles or {}, n = ix.rooms or 0, apply = map_room }) table.insert(phases, { name = "exits", files = ix.exitFiles or {}, n = ix.plain or 0, apply = map_exit }) table.insert(phases, { name = "doors", files = ix.doorFiles or {}, n = ix.doors or 0, apply = map_door }) table.insert(phases, { name = "special", files = ix.specialFiles or {}, n = ix.special or 0, apply = map_special }) -- each phase remembers how many rows precede it, so its own bar can be -- worked out from the single global counter local total = 0 for _, p in ipairs(phases) do p.base = total total = total + p.n end return phases, total end local function imp_commas(n) if type(n) ~= "number" then return "0" end local s, out = tostring(math.floor(n)), "" local c = 0 for i = string.len(s), 1, -1 do out = string.sub(s, i, i) .. out c = c + 1 if c % 3 == 0 and i > 1 then out = "," .. out end end return out end --[[ Plain text, not markup. This is only ever printed to the terminal, and it was written with · in it — which the panel renders and utilprint does not, so '/awcore import' reported "paused · 35,494 / 99,262".
